When installing a cooler make sure to apply the thermal paste on the right side

This does not necessarily kill it. Supposedly filling the socket with thermal grease used to be a thing for extreme subzero overclocking. Also, I don't think that any modern thermal compound is electrically conductive.

Right. Most sockets in really expensive computing systems (millions of dollars plus) have some sort of non-conductive paste/lube for thermal and mechanical reasons. It moves out of the way enough to make a good electrical contact, sometimes better than before applying a paste.

Or dielectric grease for below ambient cooling, which was more common on Socket 462 chips. If the cooler temp goes below room temp there is a chance of condensation forming. Dielectric grease applied in that manner will keep it out of the CPU socket.

The biggest difference, as noted throughout the thread, is that in the early days, being on the 'net was the exception rather than the rule, so the people who were here were only the ones who were willing and able to invest the time and energy necessary, so the demographics leaned toward interesting, intelligent, creative people. Now that it's the rule rather than the exception to be on the 'net, the demographics have settled to the lowest common denominator of humanity, so noxious, petulant, ill-mannered idiots are over-represented.

I miss early forums - back when I had to learn html so I could do my own markup because I wanted to be able to post more that just plain text.

I miss having control of my system and my connection. I didn't put up with spyware or auto-updating or auto-reporting or pretty much anything that interfered with full and complete control over what was happening on my system. It was such a simple and straightforward concept - this is my computer, and I control what it does and when it does it, and that's just that. And it was actually possible to do that - that was the way I spent my first years on the 'net. Now it's not only pretty much impossible, but entirely unfathomable to the newer generation - they not only don't know that anyone could do that - they don't understand why anyone would.

I started a program and told it to do its thing, and it beeped and clicked, and crackled and beeped and dialed and beeped and clicked and squaaaaaaaaaaawked and.... then a portal opened into a new and fascinating world, and I stepped through. Now I just open a window, and it's about as drab and mundane as opening any other window, and the world it gives me access to is as cheap and tawdry as a mall food court.
